questions.prompt: Which type of radiation is stopped by a single sheet of paper?
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are large and doubly charged, so they ionise strongly and lose their energy quickly. They are stopped by paper or a few centimetres of air.

questions.prompt: The activity of a radioactive sample falls from 800 Bq to 50 Bq in 12 hours. What is its half-life, in hours?
Which statements correctly describe **beta-minus** decay? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The nucleon number $A$ stays the same
A neutron in the nucleus changes into a proton
The emitted electron comes from the electron shells around the nucleus

questions.explanation: In beta-minus decay the change ${}^{1}_{0}n \rightarrow {}^{1}_{1}p + {}^{0}_{-1}e + \bar{\nu}$ happens **inside the nucleus**, so $A$ is unchanged and $Z$ rises by 1. A fall of 2 in $Z$ happens in alpha decay.

questions.prompt: Heating a radioactive sample strongly will shorten its half-life.
questions.explanation: Radioactive decay is spontaneous: it is not affected by temperature, pressure or chemical changes, so the half-life stays the same.

questions.prompt: A radioisotope has a half-life of 10 s. Find its decay constant $\lambda$ in s⁻¹ (to 3 significant figures).
An alpha particle is identical to the nucleus of which element?
questions.explanation: An alpha particle is ${}^{4}_{2}\text{He}$: two protons and two neutrons, the nucleus of a **helium** atom.
